candidates.name: guestready/airdna-api
candidates.what_it_holds: Thin client wrapper for the commercial AirDNA Enterprise API (market metrics, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates). No data committed; requires a paid AirDNA API key to pull anything. 2 stars, last updated 27 Jan 2026.
candidates.why_useful: Targets gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy for STRs) if the team ever obtains an AirDNA key; otherwise only documents the request shapes AirDNA exposes.
candidates.size_hint: no data committed; API client code only

candidates.name: subnetangel/airdna-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: FastMCP server exposing AirDNA STR market data (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR by market) to an LLM agent. Also requires a paid AirDNA subscription/API key to return anything; no data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Same AirDNA-gap relevance as above (gap #2), packaged as an agent tool rather than a raw client; still blocked on the paid key.

candidates.name: api-evangelist/airdna
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent third-party write-up/profile of the AirDNA Enterprise API surface (endpoints for market metrics, STR listing data, comparable-property sets, Rentalizer revenue estimates) with links back to airdna.co. Documentation only, no code or data committed.
candidates.why_useful: Useful only as a map of what AirDNA's paid API actually exposes, in case the team later licenses it for gap #2; adds no data itself.

candidates.name: surfnterd/pricelabs-tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Read-only daily snapshot/alerting dashboard for a SINGLE PriceLabs-managed listing: prices, booking pace, YoY comparison, reservation counts, ntfy alerts. Explicitly makes no write calls to PriceLabs. Requires the operator's own PriceLabs account/listing; no market-wide comps data, no data committed to the repo. MIT licensed, updated 8 Sep 2026 (active).
candidates.why_useful: Shows the shape of PriceLabs' own-listing pace/YoY export (relevant to gap #2 style booking-pace concepts) but is single-listing telemetry, not a market panel, and needs a paid PriceLabs subscription to run.
candidates.size_hint: code only, snapshots kept locally by the operator, not in the repo

candidates.name: tule2236/Airbnb-Dynamic-Pricing-Optimization
candidates.what_it_holds: 239-star (highest-starred repo found in this theme) business-analytics project: clustering for competitive-set analysis + kNN regression for demand forecasting + an optimization model to set nightly price, built on a scraped/exported Airbnb listings dataset (not committed as a distinct new dataset; appears to be a single-market snapshot bundled with the analysis notebooks).
candidates.why_useful: Illustrative of how a PriceLabs/Wheelhouse-style comp-set method is built, but it does not add data beyond what we already hold (Inside Airbnb-style single-market listing snapshot), so it is cataloguing value only as a method reference.
candidates.geography: single market (unspecified in search result, likely a Kaggle-style single-city Airbnb export)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Inside Airbnb single-market listing snapshots already held

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub for genuinely new data: PriceLabs/Beyond/Wheelhouse/AirDNA are all commercial SaaS products whose GitHub footprint is (a) internal-looking employee/candidate take-home-assignment repos with zero stars and no committed data (dozens seen, e.g. every 'PriceLabs-Assignment' / 'PL_Assignment' repo — excluded as noise), (b) thin API-client wrappers/MCP servers that require the caller to already hold a paid API key (AirDNA, PriceLabs) and therefore commit no data themselves, or (c) generic 'Airbnb dynamic pricing' student/portfolio ML projects that re-run clustering/kNN/regression on a single scraped or Kaggle-style listings file with no new market data (dozens seen, all low/excluded per the Kaggle-NYC exclusion rule's spirit). Found zero open-source STR pricing tools that embed or redistribute a genuine multi-market comps dataset. Rate-limit note: hit HTTP 403 'API rate limit exceeded' on the 'beyond pricing'+'wheelhouse' combined query on both the first attempt and the retry after a 40s Monitor-based wait (the shared 30/min search budget across ~10 concurrent agents was likely still saturated); per the hard-limit rule (max 6 gh search calls) I stopped rather than retry further. WebSearch fallback (site:github.com queries) was also unavailable — the session's shared 200-call WebSearch budget was already exhausted by other concurrent scouts before my calls ran, so no site:github.com queries actually executed. Net effect: this scout's coverage relies on 6 successful `gh search repos` calls plus general knowledge; a follow-up scout with a fresh WebSearch budget or after the gh rate-limit window resets could usefully re-run 'beyond pricing', 'wheelhouse pricing algorithm', 'hospitable pricing api', and 'openbnb OR opencomps STR' queries that this run could not complete. Nothing here fills a HIGH-value numbered gap; best it does is confirm gap #2 (realised ADR/occupancy) remains unfilled by any free/open GitHub source — every lead terminates at a paid AirDNA or PriceLabs API key.
